title: King Shah Bakht and his Wazir Al-Rahwan

keywords: king shah bakht and his wazir al-rahwan
full_text:
King Shah Bakht of Persia was an energetic and valiant monarch, but his fiery temper often led him to issue hasty decrees of punishment. In his court served a Grand Vizier of sublime philosophical learning named Al-Rahwan, who had resolved to train the monarch’s mind in the virtues of deliberation.

Whenever an urgent or controversial case was brought before the royal tribunal, Al-Rahwan would step forward and say: 'Sire, before the sword of judgment is drawn, listen to an ancient history of how past rulers resolved this exact dilemma with wisdom.'

For months, Al-Rahwan related a cycle of philosophical tales—tales of merchants, judges, travelers, and kings—illustrating how hasty wrath brings lifelong regret, while patient investigation reveals hidden truth.

King Shah Bakht listened with fascinated delight, finding his hasty impulses calmed and his understanding deepened with every passing narrative.

He realized that an empire cannot be sustained by the sword alone; it requires the balance of equity, the testing of evidence, and the gentle touch of mercy.

The king established a supreme council of appeal, revoked unjust decrees, and ruled for forty years in unbroken prosperity, proclaiming that his vizier Al-Rahwan’s tales had transformed a fiery conqueror into a father of his people.
moral: A wise minister uses parables of justice to guide his monarch away from hasty decisions.
